transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You should avoid any exercise for the first week after surgery. After that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening, brisk walking, or light jogging. Just avoid anything strenuous or heavy for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information! I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be able to use your eye gel as normal. If you're unsure about anything specific, just check with your GP or care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful, thanks! I’ve been noticing that I’m very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, that's actually quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Yes, that's actually quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh, and should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your operation? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's just been about a week, so that sounds reassuring. I don't have any more questions at the moment. Thank you so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again!
